subject: Acme Corp: Security/compliance follow-up & subprocessor list
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme — follow-up from today's security call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful overview. A couple follow-ups from our security team:

- Can you confirm Redwood's current SOC 2 status (Type I/II) and provide the latest report or certification?
- We need a subprocessor list (cloud providers, CDNs, analytics, monitoring, third-party vendors) and a brief description of what data each subprocessor accesses.
- Does Redwood process PHI on the hosted API? If so, do you have HIPAA BAA options or is that only available for private deployments?

I'll share our standard vendor security questionnaire but wanted to get the SOC 2 + subprocessor list first.

Appreciate a target timeline — we're trying to wrap vendor reviews by end of next week.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Security Programs, Acme Corp
security@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — follow-up from today's security call

Hi Jane,

Great speaking with you earlier. Per our discussion, next steps and items attached:

1) SOC 2: Redwood holds a SOC 2 Type II report (scope: security, availability). Attached is the latest attestation (SOC2_cert_2025.pdf). If you need a bridge letter or more detail on controls, Rishi can share control mappings.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor inventory (acme_subprocessors_v3.xlsx). It includes cloud providers, monitoring, analytics, and CDNs with the data access category column filled out. High level: primary compute and storage are AWS (us-west-2) for hosted, with optional GCP deployments per customer.

3) PHI / HIPAA: Hosted public API does not have a default HIPAA BAA. We can support HIPAA-compliant deployments and sign BAAs for Private deployments and dedicated environments — we'll need to scope the work with your legal and Rishi/Dev to confirm technical isolation and logging.

4) Questionnaire: Please send your vendor questionnaire and we'll kick off intake. We typically aim to return a completed questionnaire within 3–5 business days for standard items; more complex legal questions sometimes take longer.

Proposed timeline: I can get the SOC2 + subprocessor list to you now (attached) and we can start the questionnaire review by EOD today. Rishi, Dev — can you confirm the PHI/HIPAA notes and whether we can provide any additional environment-level details for Acme?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: acme_subprocessors_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SOC2_cert_2025.pdf (pdf stub)

Thanks Marissa — got the attachments. A few clarifications from our side after a quick scan and an internal question:

- Can you confirm which cloud providers in the spreadsheet are used for customer data storage vs telemetry/monitoring? We want explicit boundaries (e.g., S3 for customer payloads, Datadog for metrics only).
- For any third-party analytics or error tracking vendors listed, can you confirm whether they receive request/response payloads or only anonymized metadata?
- Related to PHI: our legal team prefers to see whether Redwood will sign a BAA for hosted (public) endpoints if we enforce contract and configuration restrictions. Is hosted explicitly excluded?

We're attaching our vendor questionnaire (first pass). If you can populate the security controls and subprocessors sections that would help speed things up.

Appreciate it — timeline still tight for us (end of next week).

Best,
Jane

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — follow-up from today's security call

Hi Jane — following up with the technical details Marissa requested: 

Short answers first:
- Cloud providers: AWS (primary) hosts customer payloads (S3/EBS) for hosted customers in us-west-2; GCP is used for specific private/dedicated deployments when requested. No customer payloads are routed to analytics vendors by default.
- Telemetry/Monitoring: Datadog and Honeycomb are used for metrics and tracing; those systems receive anonymized request metadata and application metrics only. Error tracking (Sentry) is configured to redact request/response bodies; PII/PII-like fields are masked at ingestion.
- Subprocessor access levels: The attached spreadsheet column "Access" indicates "Customer data", "Metadata only", or "Admin access". The current file you received lists each vendor and the access classification.
- PHI/HIPAA: Hosted public API is not covered by a standard BAA. We can sign BAAs for dedicated or private deployments where we can demonstrate environment-level isolation, encryption in transit and at rest, logging, and retention controls. For hosted customers that require HIPAA protections, we recommend Redwood Private or a dedicated contract term.

If helpful, we can produce an architecture diagram showing data flow (S3 -> inference runtime -> ephemeral caches) and a short control mapping against Acme's questionnaire. Dev — can you pull a sanitized dataflow diagram we can share?

Next steps:
1) Marissa: confirm whether Acme wants us to return the vendor questionnaire sections first or if legal prefers a call with their counsel.
2) Dev: prepare sanitized dataflow diagram and any environment screenshots (logs/retention settings) for the questionnaire.

Happy to hop on a follow-up call this week if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
